sentences.text: Satyendra vs State Of U.P. on 21 February, 2023

Author: Krishan Pahal
Bench: Krishan Pahal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 83
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 33313 of 2020
Applicant :- Satyendra

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Pankaj Lal
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.
2. Rejoinder affidavit filed today.
Taken on record.

3. Heard learned counsel for applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State.
4.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in S.T. No. 186 of 2019, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Sarai Lakhansi, District Mau, with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.
5. As per prosecution story, the applicant was married with the deceased person as per Hindu rites on 15.06.2018.
The applicant along with other members of the family are said to have subjected the deceased cruelty for demand of dowry, leading to her death on 16.01.2019.

Satyendra vs State Of U.P. on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161136383/
1 6.
Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that he has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He is nothing to do with said offence.

Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that applicant is languishing in jail since 19.01.2019, the cause of death as per the opinion of the doctor has been found to be asphyxia as a result of ante-mortem hanging.
Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that despite the said finding, the doctor has preserved the viscera for chemical analysis.
Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that applicant has no criminal antecedent and he is poor labourer languishing in jail since about last four years.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is in jail since 19.01.2019 7.

Per contra, learned A.G.A./learned counsel for the informant has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the deceased has expired within the precinct of the house of the applicant that though within a period of one year and the applicant has not offered any explanation to the cause of her death within precinct of her house.
The presumption under Section 113B of the Indian Evidence Act lies against the applicant.
8. Learned A.G.A. has also vehemently opposed the bail application but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant.

9. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the evidence on record, and also taking into consideration the fact that witness of fact have been examined and that the deceased has expired within the precincts of the house of the applicant within a period of one year.
I do not find it a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.
10. The bail application is found devoid of merits and is, accordingly, dismissed.

11. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously, preferably within a period of one year from the date of production of a certified copy of this order or as early as possible in view of the principle as has been laid down in the recent judgements of the Apex Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar Vs. State of Punjab; 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India; (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.
